questions.q: What is the main symptom of overfitting during training?
options: Training loss and validation loss both rise together
Training loss keeps falling while validation loss flattens out or rises
The optimizer refuses to take any more steps
The model's forward pass throws a shape error
questions.explain: Overfitting shows up as a growing gap between falling training loss and flat or rising validation loss — the model is learning training-specific noise rather than generalizable patterns.

questions.q: Why is `AdamW` generally preferred over passing `weight_decay` directly to plain `Adam`?
options: AdamW trains faster on every dataset
AdamW removes the need for a learning rate
AdamW decouples the weight decay step from the gradient-based update, avoiding an awkward interaction with Adam's adaptive per-parameter rates
AdamW disables dropout automatically
questions.explain: Plain Adam's weight_decay is folded into the gradient and interacts poorly with its adaptive learning rates. AdamW decouples decay from that update, which is why it's the more common default today.

The number of units in the layer
The probability that a given activation is zeroed out during training

questions.explain: p is the probability that each activation passing through the Dropout layer gets zeroed during a training forward pass.

questions.q: What happens to a `nn.Dropout` layer when the model is switched to `model.eval()`?
options: It zeroes out even more activations than during training
It is disabled — every activation passes through unchanged
It is removed permanently from the model
Nothing changes; dropout behaves identically in both modes
questions.explain: Dropout is only active during training. In eval mode it passes every activation through unchanged, which is why forgetting model.eval() before validation silently corrupts your metrics.

questions.q: A teammate validates their model without ever calling `model.eval()`. What is the most likely effect on their reported validation metrics?
options: No effect — dropout only matters for backpropagation
The validation metrics look noisier and worse than the model's true performance, because dropout is still randomly zeroing activations
The model will throw a runtime error immediately
The validation loss will always read exactly zero
questions.explain: Leaving dropout active during validation injects randomness into the forward pass, which typically makes the reported validation metrics worse and noisier than the model's actual performance.
